# Copilot Challenge – Bug Hunting Report

## Overview

GitHub Copilot generated a service for managing orders.  
However, the generated code contains several issues related to:

- Null safety
- Optional misuse
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance inefficiencies
- Architectural problems

The goal of this exercise was to identify these issues, correct them, and explain the improvements.

---

# Original Code Generated by Copilot

```java
@Service
public class OrderService {

    @Autowired
    private OrderRepository orderRepository;

    public Order createOrder(Order order) {
        order.setTotal(order.getItems().stream()
            .mapToDouble(item -> item.getPrice() * item.getQuantity())
            .sum());
        return orderRepository.save(order);
    }

    public Order getOrderById(Long id) {
        return orderRepository.findById(id).get();
    }

    public List<Order> findOrdersByCustomer(String customerName) {
        String query = "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer = '"
            + customerName + "'";
        return orderRepository.executeNativeQuery(query);
    }

    public double getTotalRevenue() {
        List<Order> allOrders = orderRepository.findAll();
        double total = 0;
        for (Order order : allOrders) {
            total += order.getTotal();
        }
        return total;
    }

    public void deleteOrder(Long id) {
        orderRepository.deleteById(id);
    }
}
```

Bug 1 – Possible NullPointerException
Problem

The method assumes that order.getItems() is never null.
If it is null, calling .stream() will cause a NullPointerException.


Fix
```java
public Order createOrder(Order order) {

    if (order.getItems() == null || order.getItems().isEmpty()) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Order must contain items");
    }

    double total = order.getItems().stream()
            .mapToDouble(item -> item.getPrice() * item.getQuantity())
            .sum();

    order.setTotal(total);

    return orderRepository.save(order);
}
```
Explanation

We validate that the order contains items before processing them.

Bug 2 – Incorrect Optional Usage
Problem
```java
orderRepository.findById(id).get();

If the order does not exist, this will throw a NoSuchElementException.
```
Fix
```java
public Order getOrderById(Long id) {

    return orderRepository.findById(id)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new RuntimeException("Order not found"));
}
```
Explanation

Using orElseThrow() ensures a clear and controlled exception.

Bug 3 – SQL Injection Vulnerability
Problem
```java
String query = "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer = '" + customerName + "'";
```
This allows SQL Injection attacks.

Fix

Repository:
```java
@Query("SELECT o FROM Order o WHERE o.customer.name = :name")
List<Order> findByCustomerName(String name);

Service:

public List<Order> findOrdersByCustomer(String customerName) {
    return orderRepository.findByCustomerName(customerName);
}
```
Explanation

Using parameterized queries prevents injection vulnerabilities.

Bug 4 – Performance Issue
Problem
```java
List<Order> allOrders = orderRepository.findAll();
```
This loads all orders into memory, which is inefficient for large datasets.

Fix

Repository:
```java
@Query("SELECT SUM(o.total) FROM Order o")
Double getTotalRevenue();
```
Service:
```java
public double getTotalRevenue() {

    Double revenue = orderRepository.getTotalRevenue();

    return revenue != null ? revenue : 0;
}
```
Explanation

The database performs the aggregation instead of the application.

Bug 5 – Architectural Problem
Problem
```java
orderRepository.deleteById(id);
```
If the order does not exist, the user receives no meaningful feedback.

Fix
```java
public void deleteOrder(Long id) {

    Order order = orderRepository.findById(id)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new RuntimeException("Order not found"));

    orderRepository.delete(order);
}
```
Explanation

We verify the existence of the resource before deleting it.

Final Corrected Service
```java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class OrderService {

    private final OrderRepository orderRepository;

    public Order createOrder(Order order) {

        if (order.getItems() == null || order.getItems().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Order must contain items");
        }

        double total = order.getItems().stream()
                .mapToDouble(item -> item.getPrice() * item.getQuantity())
                .sum();

        order.setTotal(total);

        return orderRepository.save(order);
    }

    public Order getOrderById(Long id) {

        return orderRepository.findById(id)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new RuntimeException("Order not found"));
    }

    public List<Order> findOrdersByCustomer(String customerName) {

        return orderRepository.findByCustomerName(customerName);
    }

    public double getTotalRevenue() {

        Double revenue = orderRepository.getTotalRevenue();

        return revenue != null ? revenue : 0;
    }

    public void deleteOrder(Long id) {

        Order order = orderRepository.findById(id)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new RuntimeException("Order not found"));

        orderRepository.delete(order);
    }
}
```
Unit Tests

Two basic unit tests were implemented to verify correct behavior.
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderServiceTest {

    @Mock
    OrderRepository orderRepository;

    @InjectMocks
    OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void shouldThrowExceptionWhenOrderNotFound() {

        when(orderRepository.findById(1L))
                .thenReturn(Optional.empty());

        assertThrows(RuntimeException.class,
                () -> orderService.getOrderById(1L));
    }

    @Test
    void shouldReturnTotalRevenue() {

        when(orderRepository.getTotalRevenue())
                .thenReturn(200.0);

        double revenue = orderService.getTotalRevenue();

        assertEquals(200.0, revenue);
    }
}
```
Conclusion

This exercise demonstrates that although GitHub Copilot can accelerate development, developers must still:

Review generated code carefully

Identify potential bugs

Ensure security best practices

Optimize performance

Maintain good architectural design

AI tools assist development but do not replace engineering judgment.
